title: Geometry of the pointed Galois inverse limit
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and $\Pi=\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,x)$ with its profinite topology and left action on finite geometric fibres [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Finite etale covers are objects of [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. For every open normal subgroup $N\triangleleft\Pi$, let $(Y_N,y_N)$ be a pointed connected finite etale cover identified on its geometric fibre with $(\Pi/N,N)$, with pointed transition $Y_M\to Y_N$ inducing $aM\mapsto aN$ for $M\subseteq N$. Work in compatible universes and small indexing systems [def-weil-size-convention].
The indicated pointed covers and transition maps exist. They form a small cofinal system in the category of pointed connected finite etale Galois covers, where Galois means that the group of $X$-automorphisms acts simply transitively on the geometric fibre. The system is directed by common refinements $M\cap N$, with unique pointed arrows. Its limit $T$ exists in schemes over $X$ and canonically agrees with the limit over any small cofinal system of pointed connected finite etale Galois covers. Each $Y_N$ is qcqs; each transition and structure map is finite etale and surjective. Every projection $p_N:T\to Y_N$ is affine and surjective. The compatible $y_N$ define $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ with $p_Nt=y_N$ and $vt=x$, where $v:T\to X$ is the structure map.
The scheme $T$ is nonempty, connected, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The morphism $v$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], flat and surjective [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], and weakly etale [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism]. For every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, $v^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim_N\Gamma(Y_N\times_X V,\mathcal O))$; the displayed colimit is an ind-etale $A$-algebra, that is, a filtered colimit of etale finitely presented $A$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. The singleton $\{v\}$ is a cover in $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

proof.text: Use the fully proved finite-etale equivalenceContAction and the stabilizer classification in cor-galois-open-subgroups. For a Galois cover its point stabilizer is normal: an automorphism of the cover carries the marked point to g inverse times that point and commutes with the natural G action. Conversely, for a connected cover with normal point stabilizer every point has the same stabilizer. The pointed isomorphism classification then makes its automorphism action transitive, hence it is Galois. No FLC comparison is needed. The private import of the node thm-galois-fundamental is retained as a unit-route dependency; its additional FLC clauses are not reapplied.

proof.text: The functor from the published small UniversalCover.Index to open normal subgroups sends a stage to the stabilizer of its marked point. Point preservation and naturality give monotonicity. Pointed arrows are unique by injectivity of evaluation on a connected object. For an inclusion of stabilizers construct the quotient-group map on the pointed quotient fibres and lift it using full faithfulness of equivalenceContAction. Every open normal subgroup is realized by exists_isConnected_stabilizer_eq and the preceding Galois criterion. Thus the stabilizer functor is fully faithful and essentially surjective. Its inverse equivalence E, with its counit, gives the exact quotient labels q. Transitivity, equivariance and the point equations prove the requested transition formula.

proof.text: Transitions are finite and etale by IsFinite.of_comp and Etale.of_comp applied to their composites with the stage structure map. Their source is nonempty because of the marked point and their target is connected. The image is open (etale), closed (finite), and nonempty, so it is all of the target. The same existing clopen-image argument surjective_of_nonempty_fiber proves the structure maps surjective. No trace or degree theorem is used.

proof.text: For an index j restrict the cone to Over j. This restriction is still limiting by initiality, and its structure maps to stage j are the surjective affine transitions just proved. Apply the fully proved Scheme.surjective_of_isLimit. Its proof base-changes the limit to a residue field by isLimitPullbackCone, makes every affine stage fibre nonempty, and uses Scheme.nonempty_of_isLimit. This proves every projection surjective. Reuse UniversalCover.surjective_proj for the structure map.

source.place: Tag 01Z2, lemma-limit-nonempty; constant-base specialization of the fibre-product limit identity

proof.text: The already constructed UniversalCover.pt satisfies every requested projection equation by pt_pi and the base equation by pt_proj. Its source Spec Omega has a point.

For the reindexed scheme diagram E.functor composed with UniversalCover.diagram, use the fully proved AffineOverLimit relative-spectrum construction. Evaluation preserves colimits, so its ring over U is canonically the exact colimit normalSectionDiagram. The unique isomorphism between its limiting cone and the published cone, together with the open chart of the relative spectrum, gives a chart map k into cover. AffineOverLimit.iota_pi and the evaluation-colimit comparison give every projection equation. The structure-map equation follows by composing the equation at the whole-group stage. The relative-gluing range formula identifies the range of k with the preimage of U, giving the required isomorphism by isoOfRangeEq. The stage ring maps are etale by HasRingHomProperty.appLE. Their cocone is compatible, and connectedness of the index shows every composite with a colimit inclusion is normalSectionAlgebraMap. RingHom.IndEtale.iff_exists supplies the filtered etale presentation; invariance under the canonical ULift ring equivalences proves IndEtaleAcrossUniverses.
